### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **99** documentable anchor(s).

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 026391d5d8d8e876377d19fb08a0afc038088f76`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 35 pages)`
- **53** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 026391d5d8d8e876377d19fb08a0afc038088f76` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `21885d74715b15221125f6150ae986028bf29e2b` — the merge of head `8b615d0f9c8d803812f57534f74d3f6e7edc49bc` into base `026391d5d8d8e876377d19fb08a0afc038088f76`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 21885d74715b15221125f6150ae986028bf29e2b && git checkout 21885d74715b15221125f6150ae986028bf29e2b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 026391d5d8d8e876377d19fb08a0afc038088f76 8b615d0f9c8d803812f57534f74d3f6e7edc49bc && git checkout -B drift-repro 026391d5d8d8e876377d19fb08a0afc038088f76 && git merge --no-ff 8b615d0f9c8d803812f57534f74d3f6e7edc49bc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 026391d5d8d8e876377d19fb08a0afc038088f76
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 026391d5d8d8e876377d19fb08a0afc038088f76` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `aa6bc6d91fbe2cc9fe0776477000b988b8627140`
Local-runs: none

**What was reviewed.** PR #23034 (`feat(cli): os migrate organization-ownership --apply`, draft, base `main`, head repo = base repo) at head `aa6bc6d91f` — the head the brief named; it had not moved. Three commits: `0555b80a` (the build), `3f68f15e` (merge of `origin/main` `6d7f4df3`), `aa6bc6d9` (the apply-flags test's first load moved to `beforeAll`, 14/−5 in one test file). Net three-dot diff against `origin/main` `09ef77c7`: 9 files, +1,872 / −28, all under `packages/cli` plus one changeset; no governed path (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success). Inputs: card #22937 body and all 17 comments (claim 6122368393, report 6123371167, seat review 6124036468, correction 6138559307, ruling 6138591940, PR 3 report 6140232596, PR 3 correction 6140351542, pre-landing dispatch 6146422537; no newer os-dev-report at 2026-10-13T13:52Z); card #15211 body; ADR-0131 D3/D4/D10 on `origin/main`; the PR body, file list, diff, its one bot comment (docs drift, advisory), zero reviews; the head's check-runs; for context `organization-ownership-inventory.ts`, the pre-PR command, core's `permissionSetDefinitionFromRow` / `positionDefinitionFromRow` / `convertPositionBindingRows`, `recordDataMigrationRun` / `isDataMigrationFlagVerified`, `SaveMetaItemRequestSchema`, `sys-email-template.object.ts`, and S8's branch `claude/issue-15204-s8-catalog-objects` at `23e450a6` (same merge base `6d7f4df3`).

**Check-runs on `aa6bc6d9` at 2026-10-13T13:53Z:** 39 runs — 32 `success`, 6 `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance), **1 still running: `Test Core (3/6)`**. None failed. `Check Changeset`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Build Core` are among the successes.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **CLI surface widening (`Clause-② yes`) — right.** `--apply` (boolean, default false) and `--backup-taken` (boolean, default false) are added to `os migrate organization-ownership`; the pre-PR plan path is untouched code, so the bare run stays the read-only plan. Order in `run()`: posture resolution, then `--apply` branch, then `--backup-taken` without `--apply` refused (`flag-without-apply`, exit 1) — all before any boot. In `runApply`, the backup acknowledgement is read before `bootSchemaStack`: `--backup-taken`, else a y/N prompt only when stdin is a TTY and `--json` is off; a non-interactive or `--json` run without the flag is refused (`backup-unacknowledged`, exit 1) with the platform-takes-no-backup message (D10 item 2). JSON faces: `apply_refused` / `apply_failed` / `boot_failed` keyed off `reason`. The three apply-flags cases pin exactly these (boot mock not called on both refusals; called once with `deferSchemaDdl: true, composeHostStack: true` on the accepted path). Nit, not blocking: the `--out` flag's description still reads "Where to write the plan" though `--apply` reuses it for the report file.

2. **D10 conformance of the executor — right on the fate order, the gate and the resume; wrong on two counts (B1, B2 in ③).**
   - *Attribution (fate 3)* — right. The apply passes an `AttributionSink` into the plan's own `walkNullRows`; owners come only from the inventory's anchors and, under `single`, the Default Organization; the walk is keyset-paged (id greater than the last page's id, bound as a parameter), so the per-page `UPDATE … SET organization_id = ? WHERE organization_id IS NULL AND id IN (…)` cannot shift later pages. Repeats to a fixed point with a NULL-count-must-decrease guard (`MAX_ATTRIBUTION_PASSES` 8) and blocks loudly if writes do not land. Departure rows (`sys_setting` scope=global, `sys_sharing_rule` declared-rule mirrors) are skipped by the walk and are therefore never stamped — right for PR 3's move.
   - *Authored conversion* — right under `single` (D3): `authored` rows (`managed_by` not in package/platform/system) of `sys_permission_set` / `sys_position` go through `protocol.saveMetaItem({ type, name, item, actor })` — the spec's `SaveMetaItemRequestSchema` carries exactly `type`, `name`, `item`, optional `actor` — with bodies from core's mappers and binding rows carried into `permissionSets` via `convertPositionBindingRows`. Blockers for: two rows of one name with differing bodies, a name the catalog holds with a different body, a door refusal, conflicting per-organization bindings, bindings on an undeclared position. Deactivated authored rows are reported, not converted. Authored `sys_capability` reported (fate 4). Under a wall everything is reported. Right.
   - *Rewrite (D4)* — right. Unnamed grants are named from the set row their `permission_set_id` points at, except the three never-named cases (another organization's set row, a dangling id, a name the catalog does not resolve), with `… AND (permission_set IS NULL OR permission_set = '')`. Then EVERY grant is verified (named, resolves, agrees with its id row) and every binding row's sets are verified against the position definition. `permission_set_id` stays.
   - *Mirror deletion (fate 2)* — the gate is right: `verifyReferences` is read again immediately before the first `DELETE` (the between-runs case pins it, and the dev's ablation reddened it). Binding rows are deleted only after their sets are in the position definition (`declared` fate), which is "mirrors deleted only after their conversion is verified" for the one object whose rows carry information. Catalog mirrors are selected by `managed_by IN (package, platform, system)` minus the `authored` category. **Wrong for `sys_email_template`: see B1** — the inventory gives that object no mirror selector, so the delete predicate is "every row" minus `customized = true` minus `organization_id IS NOT NULL`; a `managed_by = 'admin'` row (the object declares `admin` as its authored provenance) with NULL organization and `customized` false is deleted as a mirror. It is not re-derivable from code; D10 fate 2 does not sanction it; #15211 says stop and report any deletion outside fate 2. PR 3's own report (6140232596) measured this exact row under PR #23034 alone, and the seat's reading (6140351542) classes admin-authored rows with the promoted population. Also: the doc comment on `deletableWhere` says `CASE … END = 0` makes a NULL-evaluating category still claim the row; the SQL does the opposite (NULL → ELSE 0 → deletable). For the `notIn` categories this is harmless because `predicateSql` spells `notIn` as `IS NULL OR NOT IN`; for an `equals: true` category it is the less safe direction.
   - *Column drops (fate 1)* — right. Only `drop_column organization_id` entries that `detectManagedDrift()` proposes for the due tables, applied through `applyMigrationEntries(…, { allowDestructive: true })`; a table with rows in a named category (the `sys_metadata` promotion categories) keeps its column and is reported; "not proposed" is reported as the declaration still carrying the column. Post-S8 the four unmanaged catalog tables are never in `due` (fate 2), and the filter ignores any `drop_table` the differ might propose for them.
   - *Checkpoint and marker* — the ledger mechanics are right: each finished step writes `recordDataMigrationRun({ passed: false, applied: false, details: { checkpoint } })`, which keeps an existing `applied_at` and clears `verified_at` (the ledger's own contract); the final write sets `applied: complete` and `passed: complete && blocking === 0`, so `applied_at` is first written only when all five steps have finished and `verified_at` only when the post-check reads zero discrepancies; a blocker leaves both as they were. The checkpoint is bound to the inventory digest and discarded on a digest change; every step is conditioned on the state it changes, so a resumed or repeated run writes nothing (the byte-identical second-run case pins it). **Wrong on what "complete" certifies: see B2** — `remainingFor` counts only `rowsToAttribute`, which excludes departure rows, so a database whose `sys_setting` still holds NULL global-rung rows (and whose `sys_sharing_rule` still holds declared-rule mirrors) ends `complete: true, blocking: 0`, `verified_at` set, `notNull.willReceive: true, "every NULL row is attributed or departs"` — while nothing has departed. `TableOutcome` has no departures field, and the human face prints a table only when attributed + deleted + unattributable + remaining is non-zero, so those rows appear nowhere in the apply report except as an unlabelled `after.organizationNull` count.
   - *Transactions* — no step runs in a transaction; each `UPDATE`/`DELETE` is one statement (atomic per statement), a mirror delete that leaves rows behind throws before the next table, and the checkpoint is written only after a step finishes. That is the resumable shape D10 names, not a transactional one; D10 asks for idempotent and resumable, so right. One consequence is unmeasured: an attribution `UPDATE` that collides with a unique index over `organization_id` (a NULL-organization grant duplicating a stamped one) fails the whole 200-id chunk and aborts the run with the driver's message and no row ids or remedy.

3. **Ruling conformance.**
   - Q2 → A: right as built — a named grant whose set the catalog does not resolve blocks the rewrite and, re-read, the deletion, with one blocker line per name naming the ids and the remedy ("Declare or author the set, or remove the grants, then re-run").
   - Q1 → A: right — no boot refusal is built; the marker is the `sys_migration` row `adr-0131-organization-ownership` written through `recordDataMigrationRun`, read through `readDataMigrationFlag` / `isDataMigrationFlagVerified` (`verified_at` non-null and `blocking === 0`); `CREATION_ATTESTED_MIGRATION_IDS` untouched.
   - Q3 / Q4 → A (PR 3's): the PR half-implements neither — no template promotion, no settings move, no sharing-rule deletion (departures are never executed; only `fate === 'mirror-deletion'` tables are). Customized and organization-stamped templates are kept and reported through the mirror step's "N row(s) are not mirrors (a named category claims them) and stay" note — right. The global-rung rows and the declared-rule mirrors it does not move are **not reported** in the apply report and are counted as done by the post-check — wrong (B2). The admin-authored uncustomized NULL-organization template is **dropped**, not reported — wrong (B1).

4. **Data safety.** No write before the backup acknowledgement and the boot. Every identifier passes `Sql.q` (`SAFE_IDENTIFIER` `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`, refused otherwise) and every value is bound, `IN` lists included; no SQL is built by concatenation from data. The only destructive steps are the gated mirror delete and the drift-machinery column drop; both are reachable on a partially migrated database only through the re-read gate and the held-category check respectively. The exception is B1: a deletion of a non-mirror population without a conversion.

5. **Post-S8 correctness — right, by reading; not yet measured on the S8 tree.** The inventory, plan and apply never read the four catalog objects through the engine: the plan enumerates physical tables from the driver's catalog statement, reads columns from `pragma_table_info` / `information_schema`, and classifies by inventory row; the apply reads and writes them through the raw-SQL seam (`resolvePlannedDriverExec`). `permission_set_id` is read as text (`text(grant.permission_set_id)`), which S8's `Field.text` redeclaration does not change. The `composeHostStack` + `composeAuthGatedSecurity` boot under S8 registers the remaining security objects, and `createSecurityCatalogReader({ registry: engine.registry, metadata })` reads registry plus metadata service as its sources require. S8 touches no organization-ownership file; its `unmanaged-tables` sweep listing the four tables is `os migrate plan`'s face, not this command's. The acceptance fixture is already the post-S8 shape. The pre-landing dispatch's scratch run of the suites on this branch plus S8 (6146422537 item 2) has no report yet: NOT MEASURED.

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/22937-cli-organization-ownership-apply.md` grades `@objectstack/cli` **`minor`** and carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; the PR body's line 2 is `Clause-②: yes`. Under the WHICH LEVEL rule in `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml` an additive widening of a published package's public surface takes at least `minor`; two new accepted flags on a published CLI command are that act, so `minor` is right and `patch` would have been refused by the level axis. Nothing is removed or renamed: no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 marker is owed. `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` reads `yes (widening)` as a declared `yes` with the `widening` arm and the body's bare `yes` as a declaration; the two agree. `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head. The changeset body matches the code on every clause I read (fate order, the three never-named cases, the gate re-read, the drift machinery, the `applied_at` / `verified_at` rule, the `wx` report file) — with the one overstatement that it says rows "still need another step" are reported, which B2 shows the apply report does not do for departures.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **B1 — blocking. Deletion outside fate 2 on `sys_email_template`.** `deletableWhere` with no inventory mirror selector deletes every row not claimed by `customized = true` or `organization_id IS NOT NULL`; a `managed_by = 'admin'` (the object's authored provenance), NULL-organization, uncustomized row is deleted without promotion and without a report line. Confirmed by the PR 3 report 6140232596 ("would have been deleted as a mirror without being promoted") and by the seat's reading 6140351542 (admin-authored rows are the promoted population). The acceptance fixture has no such row (its three templates are platform-managed), so the pin is silent. Remedy inside this PR's own surface, no inventory edit: in `runMirrorDeletion` / `deletableWhere`, when the physical table carries `managed_by`, add `(managed_by IS NULL OR managed_by NOT IN ('package','platform','system'))` to the claimed set — the same `AUTHORED` boundary the catalog objects use — so those rows stay and are counted in the "not mirrors … stay" note for PR 3 to promote; add a `tpl_admin` (NULL, `managed_by 'admin'`, `customized 0`) row to the fixture and assert it survives with counts reconciling.
- **B2 — blocking. The post-check certifies a ceremony that has not finished, and the apply report does not name what it skipped.** With departures excluded from `remainingFor`, every database holding `sys_setting` global-rung rows ends `complete: true, blocking: 0` and `verified_at` set, `notNull.willReceive: true` for `sys_setting`, and the rows appear in no step note, no table line and no `advisory` count. D10 item 4 wants tables still holding NULL rows named with the remedy and left unconstrained; item 5's refusal (C8, Q1 → A) will read this very row. Remedy, also small and inside the surface: count `fateCounts.departingRows` into `remainingFor` for `attribution` (and `report`) tables so `blocking` stays non-zero and `verified_at` null until a step performs them (PR 3's `settings-move`; the sharing-rule mirrors ride D2), and carry each departure's label and row count on `TableOutcome` and the human face as its remedy. After PR 3 the same code reads zero and the marker becomes true.
- **Form, seat decision before readying:** the PR title says "PR 2 of 2" and line 1 is `Fixes #22937`, but the maintainer ruled a PR 3 of this card (6138591940, 「本卡单开 PR 3」; #23195 closed pending re-open). Landing PR 2 as written closes the card while PR 3 is still owed on it. Either line 1 becomes `Part of #22937` (a PR-body edit the role file reserves to the seat) or the seat records that the card closes at PR 2 and PR 3 is carried otherwise.
- **Dev deviations in 6123371167 — answered, none blocking:** three files beyond the claim (the one-shot family pin now drives `--apply --backup-taken --json` as a write mode under the "no seed write" and "no lifecycle sweep" pins; `schema-migrate.ts` doc comments; one e2e comment) are mechanical and inside `packages/cli`; the direct `git push` and the one lease-named force-push before the PR existed follow the role file; the model-free trailers follow AGENTS.md; the boot refusal's location was reported and ruled Q1 → A. The `aa6bc6d9` timing fix is the one the PR 3 run named as its carrier and is test-only.
- **Open questions Q1–Q4 — ruled all A (6138591940); the code conforms except B2's reporting half.** PR 3's two questions (sharing-rule mirrors ride D2; seeded uncustomized organization-stamped copies are mirrors) are the seat's answers in 6140351542 and change nothing here; note PR 2 keeps organization-stamped seeded copies (the safe direction) that PR 3 will delete after promotion.
- **Remedy-quality notes, not blocking:** (a) an authored position that is deactivated, or any authored position under a wall, still has binding rows, and `verifyReferences` then blocks with "The authored-conversion step carries them; resolve its blocker" although that step only reported — the operator's real remedy (remove the binding rows, or activate the position) is not said; (b) the attribution unique-index collision described in ①2 aborts with the driver's error and no ids; (c) the `CASE … END = 0` comment contradicts the SQL; (d) the `--out` description.
- **Out of scope, named:** a `sys_metadata` table with organization-scoped presentational rows holds its column-drop until a promotion step that lives outside this ceremony exists, so the ceremony cannot complete there; the blocker says "resolve them, then re-run" without naming the command. The sys_metadata family's declarations on `main` still carry the column, so on today's `main` those drops are reported "not proposed" (the dev's smoke run saw this).
- **NOT MEASURED:** `test/json-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts` (comment-only edit, nightly tier — the dev said so); the full `@objectstack/cli` suite and the derived gates on the branch-plus-S8 scratch tree (dispatched 6146422537, unreported); the PostgreSQL and MySQL dialect paths of the apply (the fixture is SQLite; the dev's smoke was SQLite); the real metadata door accepting a position whose `permissionSets` names a set saved in the same run; the unique-collision case; `Test Core (3/6)` still running at 2026-10-13T13:53Z.

Adopted by `domain:engine` seat 2 at 2026-10-13T13:56Z, after a tool-use audit of the isolated reviewer's transcript: reads, `git fetch` into a review ref, and record writes only. It made no GitHub write and ran no build, test or gate. The seat takes B1 and B2 as blocking, and the dev fixes both in PR 2. Form, decided by the seat: PR 2 does not close the card while PR 3 (ruling 6138591940, 「本卡单开 PR 3」) is owed. Line 1 becomes `Part of #22937`, the title says PR 2 of 3, and PR 3 carries `Fixes #22937`. A delta record runs on the fixed head.

Reviewed-by: `session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX`

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8b615d0f9c8d803812f57534f74d3f6e7edc49bc`
Local-runs: none

**What was reviewed.** Delta record on PR #23034 (`feat(cli): os migrate organization-ownership --apply`, draft, base `main`, head repo = base repo, title now "PR 2 of 3", line 1 `Part of #22937`) at head `8b615d0f9c`, the head the brief named; it had not moved. The delta since the FAIL head `aa6bc6d91f` is ONE commit, `8b615d0f9c` ("the ceremony keeps every admin-authored fate-2 row and counts unrun departures as remaining"), 3 files, +68 / −14, no merge of `main` in between (the merge-base with `origin/main` is still `6d7f4df3c`, so the head does not carry S8 `66949b7729`). The PR's merge ref `21885d7471` (parents `026391d5d8` = `origin/main`, `8b615d0f9c`) carries S8, merges clean (no conflict markers in the PR's files), and its diff against `origin/main` is byte-equal to the three-dot diff: 9 files, +1,927 / −29 (1,956 changed lines, under 3,000), all under `packages/cli` plus one changeset; no governed path (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success). Inputs: the FAIL record 6147223040 in full; on card #22937 the ruling 6138591940, the correction 6140351542, the dispatch 6146422537, the pre-landing report 6150092087, the collection 6150126995 and the services pointer 6147942984; the PR body, file list, net diff and delta, its two comments (the docs-drift bot, the FAIL record) and zero reviews; `docs/adr/0131-*.md` on `origin/main` (D10 and the fates); the inventory on `origin/main` (blob `e3dc4afa`, identical on head); for the S8 question `packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `security-catalog.ts`, `migration-flag.ts`, `sys-email-template.object.ts` on `origin/main`, `sys-position-permission-set.object.ts` at the merge-base, and the 18 commits `main` gained since `6d7f4df3c`; the head's check-runs. The B1/B2 round's own report is not posted; the check-runs stand in for it.

**Check-runs on `8b615d0f9c` at 2026-10-13T16:45Z:** 39 — 30 `success`, 6 `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix row, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance), **3 still running: `Test Core (2/6)`, `Test Core (3/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)`.** None failed. Among the successes: `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Test Core (1/6)`, `Test Core (5/6)`, `Test Core (6/6)`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`. The typecheck and build successes are on the merge ref, so the apply's four core imports (`createSecurityCatalogReader`, `permissionSetDefinitionFromRow`, `positionDefinitionFromRow`, `convertPositionBindingRows`) resolve on post-S8 `main`; I also read them exported at `packages/core/src/security/index.ts` lines 248, 264, 281 and 285. The verdict below is conditional on the three running shards: a red one voids it.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **B1 — fixed, and inside fate 2. Right.**
